Euler--Maclaurin and uniform smooth Riemann sums establish the finite-size first-order correction. Exact cancellation has G_c=0 and G_cc=-u_* D_prime(a_0)>0, so its second correction and s=3/4 phase follow. The 45-assertion checker confirms finite identities and asymptotic numerics without being used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The deterministic centering needed for Gaussian inference shifts by N^(s-1), which meets the N^-1/2 stochastic scale precisely at s=1/2. At the uniquely motivated cancellation threshold the first bias disappears and the next unavoidable term reaches that scale at s=3/4. These are explicit model-dependent accuracy boundaries, not merely a standard CLT or arbitrary finite parameter slice.
